rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a compositional change (substituting Mo with Nb), whereas the hidden target uses thermomechanical processing (cold rolling and annealing) to modify the same alloy system. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature compression tests on as-fabricated alloys, while the target uses room-temperature tensile tests on cold-rolled and annealed material. The testing mode (compression vs. tension) and processing history differ, placing them in different regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced electronegativity difference to ease dislocation motion and improve plasticity, while the target relies on work hardening, dislocation accumulation, texture, and subsequent recovery/recrystallization. These are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts retained high compressive yield strength (~1719 MPa) with improved ductility, whereas the target reports tensile strength changes (increase with rolling, decrease with annealing) and elongation changes, with a much lower baseline strength and different property direction for the primary intervention.
